findings.evidence: The critique's finding 1 is CONFIRMED and is the single most important thing in the report: the spec's premise is false. Independently reproduced. `grep -n 'component-rule-seams\|card-creator-environment-optional' package.json` returns exactly one line each, both inside `test:contracts`, and `test` chains `npm run test:contracts`. Ran both files directly: `node tests/suite-wiring.test.mjs` prints 'suite wiring test ok: 332 test files wired into npm scripts' (it fails the build on any unwired tests/*.test.mjs, itself included), `component-rule-seams.test.mjs` prints '# pass 1 # fail 0', and `card-creator-environment-optional.test.mjs` prints 'card creator environment test ok'. The spec's Dangers bullet, DoD item 7, AC 9, the Test-shape wiring clause and the OUT/IN row 'Wiring the two orphaned guard files into an npm script' therefore describe work that is already done and cannot be IN scope. Verification verdict: CONFIRMED, no correction.

The critique's finding 2 is CONFIRMED and I proved it by execution rather than by reading. Baseline: `node tests/debt-baseline.test.mjs` prints 'debt baseline ok: 3 oversized file(s) and 41 oversized function(s), 24 inherited entries, shape gate green' (exit 0). Experiment A — added the minimum a 'new component' costs to components/settings/preset-manager-form.tsx (one import line + one JSX line rendering it, +2 lines): the gate fails with `AssertionError: components/settings/preset-manager-form.tsx:PresetManagerFormView grew to 74 lines, past its recorded baseline of 73` (tests/debt-baseline.test.mjs:225). Experiment B — appended the kind word to the existing meta line in components/settings/preset-manager-list.tsx, a NET ZERO line change (1 insertion, 1 deletion): the gate still fails, with a different assertion, `the inherited debt set changed; a split or a new violation must be recorded here`, and the diff shows the missing row `+ 'components/settings/preset-manager-list.tsx:PresetManagerList#1: 74 lines (baseline 74)'`. Both files restored (`git status --porcelain` shows only the pre-existing untracked docs/runs/card_1fgz8lge/; `git diff --stat` empty). One correction to the critique, in the spec's disfavour: finding 2 says the list indicator 'costs >=1 line'. The truth is stronger and worse — ANY edit to preset-manager-list.tsx fails the gate, because check-source-budgets.mjs reports the oversized function as 'inherited' only when it appears in the changed set, and the inherited list must equal tests/debt-baseline.test.mjs's inheritedBaseline verbatim (assert.deepEqual at :252). Neither preset-manager-form.tsx:PresetManagerFormView nor preset-manager-list.tsx:PresetManagerList appears in inheritedBaseline. So the spec's core architectural claim ('It must be a new component, not a block inside PresetManagerFormView: that function is at exactly 73 lines') is not merely insufficient — it is irrelevant. Extracting PresetManagerFormBody and PresetManagerPresetRow, adding both entries to inheritedBaseline in the gate's print order (alphabetical: after plugin-update-status.tsx, before preset-onboarding.tsx), and lowering both ceilings in scripts/source-debt.json is not one option among several, it is the only path that leaves the gate green.

The critique's finding 4 is CONFIRMED, verified from both ends. Document: DoD item 5 (spec-product.md:206-207) reads 'No card ever lands in a different checkout than the one its dialog showed, with no notice', and AC 6 (:232-234) accepts exactly that case ('the environment the card lands in is the exploratory workspace's'). Code: server/cards-create.ts:249-252 is `const environment = workspace.exploratory ? workerEnvironment(workspace.source, params, true) : selectCardEnvironment(input.environment, workerEnvironment(workspace.source, params));` — the exploratory branch never consults input.environment. The notice writer bails first: server/cards-create-persist.ts:118 is `if (workspace.exploratory) return;`. And the substitution is real, not theoretical: workerEnvironment(..., forceWorkspaceHost=true) returns `{type:'host', hostId: source.hostId, workspace:{type:'unmanaged', path: source.path}}` (server/workers.ts:99-101), which describeCardEnvironment labels 'shared' (lib/tracks.mjs:100-101) — so a worktree preset on a personal project lands the card in the shared checkout, with no log, no comment, no signal. DoD 5 and AC 6 cannot both stand. Also confirmed the reachability narrowing: server/cards-create.ts:131-134 throws for a build card on proj_personal, so only research/explore reach it.

The critique's finding 12 (R3 is not a genuine unknown) is CONFIRMED and I consider it stronger than 'medium'. Independent read: components/panels/build-panel.tsx:81 is `onOpenPresets={() => props.setPresetsOpen(true)}`, :119 is `const [presetsOpen, setPresetsOpen] = useState(false)`, and renderPresetManager is handed to the host at :94 (the critique says :93, which is renderOnboarding — a one-line slip) as `renderPresetManager={props.renderPresetManager}`. PresetManagerProps (components/panels/build-panel-dialogs.tsx:17-23) is exactly `{open, onOpenChange, rpc, presets, onChanged}` — no projectId. PresetManagerDialogProps (components/settings/preset-manager-shell.tsx:22-28) likewise. The list is fed by `rpc.call('listPresets', {})` (components/panels/build-panel-state.ts:165), which is board-global. R3 asks whether research/explore on a personal project should hide the control; the control's container has no concept of a project, so the question is unanswerable as posed. The spec's own SCOPE READING assumption (frontmatter) already fixed the preset as global. R3 should be dropped or reframed as the copy question it actually is.

The critique's finding 22 is CONFIRMED by direct schema execution, not by reading. Loaded server/platform-rpc-contract.ts:platformRpcContract.upsertPreset.input through the repo's own TS register and parsed two payloads: OMITTING environmentKind -> success:true, parsed as "project-default"; passing environmentKind:'local' -> REFUSED with 'environmentKind: Invalid option: expected one of "project-default"|"new-worktree"'. server/preset-handler-crud.ts:84 then writes `input.environmentKind` into the UPDATE's values array (:89-96) with no presence check, in contrast to baseBranch/machineId which use `?? null` (:85-86). So any caller that omits the field — a stale bundled client, a future CLI writer, the automation path — silently converts a worktree preset into a checkout preset on its next save, with no error and no log. The critique's 'low' severity is arguably right (it is a latent robustness gap, not a current-path break) but its sub-claim that the spec's 'no contract change' framing covers this is not: removing .default(...) IS a contract change and must be declared as one.

The critique's finding 7 is CONFIRMED and is the sharpest reframing in the report. Read lib/tracks.mjs:94-101: `if (exploratory) return 'exploratory'; if (envType === 'project-default') return 'managed'; if (workspaceType === 'managed-worktree') return 'worktree'; if (workspaceType === 'personal') return 'personal'; if (workspaceType === 'unmanaged') return 'shared';`. The 'worktree' label is reachable ONLY for host + managed-worktree. Confirmed: tests/tracks.test.mjs:51-54 pins exactly this table, including `describeCardEnvironment({exploratory:false, envType:'project-default'}) === 'managed'`. The spec's Dangers bullet (:165-167) reads 'A seeded card stores worktree where it previously stored managed/shared' — phrased as a one-time migration. It is not one-time; it is per-path and permanent. A composer-started card (which will now submit host+managed-worktree) stores 'worktree'; an auto-started GitHub card, a CLI-drafted card, or a research-fanout card never sets input.environment (server/github-automation-rules.ts:145, server/runtime/cli/cli-split.ts:255, server/runtime/research-fanout.ts:102 per the critique) and takes the selectCardEnvironment(undefined, workerEnvironment(...)) branch, storing 'shared' or 'managed'. Same preset, two labels, forever — sitting directly under DoD 5. The spec must restate the bullet as a per-path divergence and decide whether describeCardEnvironment should prefer preset intent over submitted shape.

The critique's finding 6 (built-in kind cascade) is CONFIRMED end to end, and the mechanism is worse than a simple inheritance because it is a two-hop cascade with an OR condition. server/preset-lookups.ts:114-120 firstWorktreePreset: `SELECT id FROM presets WHERE environment_kind = 'new-worktree' ORDER BY is_default DESC, name ASC LIMIT 1` — a built-in flipped to new-worktree becomes this row. It feeds resolveWorktreePreset (server/github-automation-context.ts:89-92) and, via effectiveBuildEnvironmentKind (:121-131), the automation gate's worktreePresetId argument. lib/github-automation-gate.mjs:25-30 resolveEffectiveEnvKind: `if (bandEnvKind === 'new-worktree' || bandEnvKind === 'project-default') return bandEnvKind; ... if (typeof worktreePresetId === 'string' && worktreePresetId) return 'new-worktree';` — so flipping a built-in un-parks every rule that was parked for want of a worktree preset, globally, for every project. Then components/settings/preset-manager-form-state.ts:68-72 defaultForm spreads formFromPreset(preset) over presets.find(isDefault) ?? presets[0] and clears only id and name, so it becomes the inherited kind of every preset created afterwards. AC 4 blesses built-in round-tripping while noticing none of this. Confirmed independently: no project-scoping, no band guard, no confirmation. The control should be disabled when preset.builtIn, or an AC plus a FEATURES.md paragraph must name the cascade.

The critique's finding 16 is CONFIRMED and corrects the spec on a factual point. The spec's Dangers bullet (:168-170) says components/isolated-worktree-check.tsx:13 'tells the reader they must go elsewhere for something they can now make here'. Read the actual constant (components/isolated-worktree-check.tsx:13): 'Needs a New-worktree preset in Agent Presets - without one the card parks with an explanation instead of starting in your checkout.' It names Agent Presets as the place — which is exactly where the new control lands — so it stays TRUE after this change. The 'created elsewhere' framing is false, and DoD item 6 (:208-209) inherits it. Also verified the FEATURES.md side: :1206-1207 says 'environment kind stays a preset field' (an under-description, not a falsehood) and :1012-1013 says 'environment, branch forwarded unchanged; Stelow never re-picks it' (genuinely becomes incomplete). And the echo sites are wider than the spec's single file: `grep -rn 'New-worktree preset' server/ lib/ components/` returns server/github-issue-flow.ts:213 and :232, server/github-rule-rpcs.ts:91, lib/github-automation-gate.mjs:34, components/github/github-automation-tab.tsx:76, plus server/runtime/shared-checkout.ts:10, lib/shared-checkout-exposure.mjs:10 and components/detail/file-occupancy.tsx:18 as comments. tests/server-github-issue-flow.test.mjs:107 and :127 pin two of those sentences by regex ('Create a New-worktree preset in Agent Presets', 'Choose a New-worktree preset'), so editing that copy is a test change, not a one-line edit. The spec names one file; the work is at least six plus two test pins.

The critique's finding 21 is CONFIRMED by inspecting the SDK's own export surface. node_modules/@get-bb/plugin-sdk/bundled-types/bb-plugin-sdk-app.d.ts:368 declares `type CreateThreadEnvironmentArgs = z.infer<typeof createThreadEnvironmentArgsSchema>;` with no `export` keyword. The file has exactly two export statements (lines 3025 and 3026); I grepped the full export-type list and CreateThreadEnvironmentArgs is absent from both. So the spec's prescribed signature 'presetKind -> CreateThreadEnvironmentArgs | undefined' in lib/ cannot be written literally — the name is not importable. The critique's workaround is also verified as the house pattern: lib/ has 198 .mjs and 196 hand-written .d.mts siblings, tests/declaration-surface.test.mjs enforces that a declared name is actually bound in the sibling module, and lib/card-environment.mjs / lib/card-environment.d.mts is exactly the pure-mapping-with-hand-written-declaration shape the spec wants (selectCardEnvironment, isManagedWorktreeEnvironment, environmentFallbackNotice — all typed as `unknown` in the .d.mts precisely because the SDK types are unreachable). Additional verified fact supporting the critique: no lib/*.mjs currently imports the SDK at all (`grep -rln '@get-bb/plugin-sdk' lib/` returns nothing), so this would be the first. Name lib/preset-environment-seed.mjs, return NonNullable<NewThreadComposerProps['defaultEnvironment']> — a type that IS exported at line 3026 — and ship the .d.mts.

The critique's finding 15 is CONFIRMED with one mechanical correction and one quantitative correction. Read components/settings/preset-manager-list.tsx:41-46: `<span className='min-w-0 flex-1 truncate'>` wraps the name plus the meta line; :48-51 the two conditional Pills (default, built-in); :52-81 `<div className='flex shrink-0 gap-1'>` with up to three Buttons. truncate is white-space:nowrap, so a block child added inside that span never renders as a second line. Correction on the mechanism: it is CLIPPED, not ellipsised — the ellipsis applies to the container's own inline overflow, while a nested block child is cut by it. Same conclusion, different words, and the spec should say 'clipped'. Quantitative correction: :30 is `max-h-56` = 224px and rows are ~38px + 6px gap, so roughly 5 rows are visible today, not ~3 as the critique states; the spec should state the real visible-row cost of the per-row addition. The house pattern for a scrollable option list does carry a fade — components/settings/preset-assign-options.tsx:173-191 useScrollFade and :204-219 render the gradient overlay — and this list has neither. Recommended: append the kind word to the existing meta line (no growth), or render a Pill only when environmentKind === 'new-worktree' with absence meaning checkout, and state that the row owns this fact.

The critique's finding 13 is CONFIRMED with a scope correction. components/ui/ contains no radio or two-option primitive — only button, card, coarse-pointer-sizing, dialog, drawer-keyboard-styles, hooks/, icon, input, mobile-trigger, motion, overlay-trigger, persistent-drawer-focus, persistent-responsive-drawer-shell, persistent-overlay-context, responsive-drawer-shell, responsive-overlay, strip-radix-content-props. The two in-repo implementations genuinely disagree: components/creation/strategy-picker.tsx:68-79 puts focus-within:outline focus-within:outline-2 focus-within:outline-primary on the label with an sr-only radio (:77) and a fieldset + sr-only legend (:103-104); components/settings/preset-assign-options.tsx:83-89 uses a visible `accent-primary` radio, and grep for focus-visible|focus-within|outline across that whole file returns NOTHING. So strategy-picker is the only one of the two yielding WCAG 2.2 focus appearance today. Correction: 'neither component is exported' holds for the row helpers (StrategyOptionRow:64, PresetOptionRow:64, both module-private) but not for the main exports — StrategyPicker:127 and PresetAssignOptions:224 are both exported, so reuse would mean extracting the row, not importing it. The spec argues DRY only for placement and never for visual form; it should name the shape it copies and state that extraction is out of scope.

The scaffolding facts underlying findings 14, 18, 19 and 20 are CONFIRMED, with line corrections. preset-manager-form.tsx:10 declares `busy: boolean`, :84-86 `<Button size='sm' disabled={busy}>` with a 'Working…' label, :33 the body draws its own surface (`mt-3 rounded-md border bg-muted/30 p-3`), imports at :4-5, JSX body :59-76. preset-manager-crud.ts:78 sends `environmentKind: state.form.environmentKind` in the upsert payload, :88 writes `error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Save failed.'` verbatim into the single message field, :64-67 is the hand-written 'Name is required.' refusal. preset-manager-types.ts:8 declares `environmentKind: string` on the listed preset type (the union is at :20), :48-49 casts `preset.environmentKind as PresetManagerForm['environmentKind']` unchecked — and :46-47 does the same unchecked cast for permissionMode, which the critique did not mention. Correction: EMPTY_PRESET_FORM starts at preset-manager-types.ts:29, not :36; :36 is its `environmentKind: 'project-default'` value. preset-assign-options.tsx:11 PresetSummary does carry `environmentKind: string`, and the option subtitles print provider/model only — but at :156, :252 and :261, not :265-272. The decisive fact for findings 19 and 20: `grep -rn environmentKind components/` outside the type declarations and the CRUD payload returns exactly two hits, both non-rendering (preset-assign-options.tsx:11 the type, preset-manager-crud.ts:78 the payload). environmentKind is today carried end-to-end and surfaced in no user-facing string anywhere.

The critique's finding 17 is CONFIRMED. server/workers.ts:94-104 workerEnvironment is still the sole consumer of preset.environment_kind on every path that sends no explicit environment, and those paths are not dead: the respawn fallback is workers.ts:194-206 fallbackEnvironment, which calls workerEnvironment(source, params, card.workspace_kind === 'exploratory') and is reached from the fresh()/respawn chain at :295-302 (`const effective = deps.getReliablePreset(...)` then `respawn(deps, cardId, effective.id, reason)`), covering a card parked in the Bucket and started later. A preset swap also re-enters it: server/preset-handler-assignments.ts:60-77 assignPreset -> refreshRestartPending(db, card.id, card.worker_thread_id, card.worker_preset_id, presetId). None of these paths writes a substitution notice: the only notice site is server/cards-create-persist.ts:118-122, which is create-time and returns early for exploratory workspaces. The spec's Problem section calls workerEnvironment 'dead code on the main path' and lists changing workers.ts:103 as OUT. 'Dead on the composer path' is accurate; 'dead' is not. The spec should either accept the consequence explicitly or give those paths an observable trail comment, plus an AC naming the worktree a Bucket-started, imported, or CLI-drafted card lands in.

The critique's findings 10, 11 and 12 (R1, R2, R3) are CONFIRMED as a group. R1: its stated fallback is 'fall back to seeding nothing and saying so', but AC 1 (:215-218) requires unconditionally that 'submitting untouched creates a card whose stored environment label is worktree' — unachievable for a non-Git source under that fallback. Worse, R1 re-asks a question the SDK already answers at bb-plugin-sdk-app.d.ts:2645-2647: 'A host environment whose host no longer exists - or whose project has no source on it - falls back to the composer's default host'. The spec never says that fallback is silent. R2: its default is 'Default to documenting host semantics', which satisfies AC 7 (a FEATURES.md note) but directly contradicts DoD item 4 ('Picking something else in the picker always wins') and AC 2. The trigger is in-product, not hypothetical: build-panel.tsx:145 openPresets is `() => setPresetsOpen(true)` with no setCreateOpen(false), and build-panel-dialogs.tsx:88-102 (CreateBuildDialog) and :112-118 (renderPresetManager) both render in the same fragment, so a preset save fires onChanged -> `await props.state.load()` (build-panel.tsx:92) -> loadBuildData replaces data.boardPresets (build-panel-state.ts:171) -> analysisPreset returns a new row (:226-232) under a live composer. The SDK docstring at :2608-2625 states the rule: the default* props are value-compared each render and when any changes after mount the composer re-seeds EVERY execution and environment selection, including ones the user had already touched. R2's own suggestion — a value-stable seed computed once per dialog mount — is the mitigation and should be promoted from spike to committed decision. R3 is unanswerable for the reason given in verify-preset-manager-has-no-project-scope above.

The critique's finding 5 is CONFIRMED, with a caveat about its own evidence base. The spec's table (:104-107) pairs stored 'project-default' with the label 'Project checkout' while omitting the seed prop. The SDK states what omission yields (bb-plugin-sdk-app.d.ts:2651-2652): '{ type: "project-default" } seeds nothing; the composer resolves its own default and submits that concrete environment instead' — so omitting is correct, and the resulting label is whatever the composer resolves, which lib/tracks.mjs:96-101 maps to 'managed' (envType project-default) or 'shared' (host+unmanaged), never to a word the reader can tie to 'Project checkout'. Caveat the critique should carry: its supporting citation for 'BB's project-default now resolves to a fresh managed worktree' is bb commit 893a05a, which is NOT in this repository — `git log -1 893a05a` returns 'ambiguous argument', and grep finds the SHA only inside the stelow artifacts themselves (state.md:117, runs/exec_x0bt01c3/recon/shape.md:40,140, runs/exec_x0ctpt5p/strategic/context-analysis.md:330 which cites get-bb/bb 'Allow Tasks dispatch without requiring Git (#1396)'). The load-bearing vocabulary claim of the whole spec therefore rests on an unverifiable external SHA, and the spec cites it as settled fact. That is itself a finding: a spec whose central premise is an unpinned external commit should say so. The label mismatch stands regardless of which resolution bb chose.

The critique's findings 8 and 9 are CONFIRMED and I strengthened finding 9 with a schema execution. The stored kind arrives as a plain string (components/settings/preset-manager-types.ts:8; RPC output z.string() at server/platform-rpc-contract.ts:80) and is cast unchecked into the union at preset-manager-types.ts:48-49. Out-of-enum values are reachable on two paths: server/preset-migrations.ts:11 gives fresh installs `environment_kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'project-default' CHECK (environment_kind IN ('project-default','new-worktree'))`, but the upgrade path at :53-59 adds the column as `['environment_kind', 'TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'project-default']` — no CHECK, confirmed by reading the additions array. And server/runtime/cli/cli-draft.ts:100-102 casts the flag blind: `environmentKind: (flag('--workspace') ?? 'project-default') as 'project-default' | 'new-worktree'`, then calls deps.presets.handlers.upsertPreset(input) directly at :107. On the client side, the RPC input enum (platform-rpc-contract.ts:100) does refuse an out-of-enum value at host validation — I confirmed the message is the raw enum text 'Invalid option: expected one of "project-default"|"new-worktree"' — and preset-manager-crud.ts:88 writes error.message verbatim into the form's single message line. Contrast the one hand-written refusal in the same function, 'Name is required.' at :64-67. So the failure mode is a raw schema string in a sentence slot. Both halves need work: a client-side check in savePreset with a reader-facing refusal naming both options (keeping enum + CHECK as defence in depth), and normalisation in formFromPreset so an unknown kind leaves the radio group in an explicit unrecognised state instead of with nothing checked.

The critique's findings 20 and 25 are CONFIRMED. Finding 20: the composer names the active preset but not its kind. Verified at components/creation/create-build-dialog.tsx:119 — `lines={[`Analysis phase runs on ${analysisName}`]}` with analysisName = analysisPreset?.name ?? 'Default' (:173). The research and explore twins do the same at :96 each (name plus a '(board default)' marker). The prop types at create-build-dialog.tsx:134, create-research-dialog.tsx:110 and create-explore-dialog.tsx:110 are all `{providerId, modelId, reasoningLevel, permissionMode, name}` — environmentKind absent from all three, exactly as the spec says. Note the critique cited the file as components/panels/create-build-dialog.tsx; the real path is components/creation/ (components/panels/create-build-dialog.tsx does not exist). Consequence: a reader who meets a seeded worktree picker has no way to learn a preset chose it, and the highest-consequence field in the form (where the agent works) is given the same unspecified weight and position as a free-text name inside a two-row collapsed body. Finding 25: tests/card-design-tokens.test.mjs:35-39 walks components/**/*.tsx recursively, so a new PresetEnvironmentKindField is inside the gate; any text-[Npx] must be a named step of lib/design-tokens.ts TYPE_SCALE or an entry in TYPE_EXCEPTIONS (currently three: text-[10px] literal model id, text-[15px] card request text, text-[9px] superscript annotation). The spec names no token for the group label or help line, and does not say whether the field is form content composing with the existing body surface (preset-manager-form.tsx:33) or a new SECTION_SURFACE — which also puts it inside tests/card-surface-consistency.test.mjs.

Overall assessment of the upstream critique as an artifact. The upstream verdict 'needs-revision' is CORRECT and should stand. All 25 findings were checked; none was fabricated. 22 are confirmed with no material correction, 3 carry line-reference or magnitude slips (list rows ~5 not ~3 and clipped-not-ellipsised; renderPresetManager at :94 not :93; EMPTY_PRESET_FORM at :29 not :36; assign-option subtitles at :156/:252/:261 not :265-272; create-build-dialog is under components/creation/ not components/panels/; 'neither component is exported' is true of row helpers but not the main exports; the form's message+Close/Save live at :77-87 so the body proper ends at :76), and 1 (label-project-checkout-unearned) is confirmed on its conclusion while its external-SHA evidence base should be flagged as unverifiable in-repo. The two most consequential findings — the false orphan-tests premise and the source-ceiling blocker — were independently proven by execution, and the second turned out stronger than the report stated. The report's weaknesses are presentation-only: the evidence strings pack 6-8 file:line citations plus a recommendation into single fields, which makes each one hard to check without redoing the work, and the priority ordering interleaves severities. Neither affects the verdict. One observation about the report's own framing: it offers no ordering for remediation, and findings 1, 2 and 22 are prerequisites (delete the false DoD/AC, extract the two components and amend the ledger, decide the enum default) that must land before any of the medium findings are actionable.

questions.question: The RPC input's .default('project-default') means a caller that omits environmentKind silently downgrades a worktree preset on its next save. Removing .default(...) is a contract change, which the spec explicitly says it is not making. Which is it: (a) drop the default so absence is a loud refusal, or (b) keep it and add a tests/server-presets.test.mjs contract test asserting a stored new-worktree preset re-saved without the field stays new-worktree? The spec must declare which, because 'no contract change' cannot be true under (a).

lib/tracks.mjs:94-101 can label the same worktree preset 'worktree' on the composer path and 'shared'/'managed' on every auto-start, CLI, research-fanout, Bucket-respawn and preset-swap path. Is that divergence acceptable (and then DoD 5 must be restated as a per-path guarantee), or should describeCardEnvironment be changed to prefer the preset's intent over the submitted shape? This decision changes what FEATURES.md:1008-1013 is allowed to claim, so it cannot wait for implementation.

Editing a built-in preset's kind cascades globally: it becomes firstWorktreePreset, un-parks every GitHub automation rule that was parked for want of a worktree preset (lib/github-automation-gate.mjs:25-30), and becomes the inherited kind of every preset created afterwards (preset-manager-form-state.ts:68-72). Should the kind control be disabled for built-ins, or allowed with an explicit AC and a FEATURES.md paragraph naming the cascade?

The meta span at preset-manager-list.tsx:41-46 is truncate, so a second line can never render, and the list is max-h-56 (~5 visible rows) with no scroll fade. Which form does the kind take: the kind word appended to the existing meta line (no growth, no new element), or a Pill rendered only when environmentKind === 'new-worktree' with absence meaning checkout?

DoD 4 and AC 2 require that a human pick always wins, but the spec's R2 defaults to documenting the host's re-seed behaviour, and the trigger is reachable in-product (openPresets leaves the create dialog mounted; a save replaces data.boardPresets under a live composer). Is the committed mitigation a value-stable seed computed once per dialog mount (R2's own suggestion, promoted from spike), with AC 7 demoted to a fallback if the composer is later observed re-seeding on a stable value?

There is no shared two-option primitive and the two in-repo implementations disagree, with only components/creation/strategy-picker.tsx yielding WCAG 2.2 focus appearance today. Which shape does PresetEnvironmentKindField copy, and is extracting a shared radio confirmed out of scope for this cycle?
